what: the bounded three-solve coupled chip-cell numerical-method pilot
approved_by: the repository owner, in the checkpoint-A review thread

constraints.external_or_additional_compute: none; one job on the standard GitHub-hosted runner
constraints.p3_halo_choice: 0.12 mm, chosen so that every run stays inside the existing 250 000 DOF rule; the 0.15 mm variant, which would have needed a one-run exception, was declined

note: Committing this file on a palace/** branch starts the pilot. It is the approval record and the trigger at once, so a pilot cannot be started by an unrelated code change.

reruns.solves: all three completed; Palace's own output is in that run's log
reruns.why_rerun: a defect in the runner, not in the science: the container was launched without a --user flag, so Palace wrote postpro/ as root and git could not unlink those files during the rebase, leaving the record uncommitted. The approved pilot is unchanged and is re-run to preserve the evidence in the repository.
reruns.fixed_by: scripts/palace_coupled_pilot.py now passes --user, as the main Palace adapter already did
